record.original_question: Let D1 and D2 be bounded Jordan domains, bounded by curves C1 and C2 of bounded boundary rotation (in the sense of Paatero, see e.g. Noonan [607]); then C1 and C2 are rectifiable, and we shall assume that they have the same length. It is known that in this case, every isometric sewing is conformally admissible and generates a Riemann surface which is equivalent to a sphere S. It follows from results of Aleksandrov (no citation) and Reshetnjak (no citation) that the curve C on S which corresponds to C1 (and C2 ) is of bounded boundary rotation. Can one find a function-theoretic proof of this? (A. Huber)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A bounded Jordan domain D in the plane is said to have boundary of bounded boundary rotation (in the sense of Paatero) if the bounding Jordan curve is rectifiable and the total variation of the direction angle of its tangent (suitably interpreted for curves that need not be smooth) is finite.

Let D₁ and D₂ be two bounded Jordan domains whose boundary curves C₁ and C₂ both have bounded boundary rotation in the Paatero sense, and assume that C₁ and C₂ have the same (finite) length L. Choose an isometric identification φ: C₁ → C₂, that is, a homeomorphism that preserves arclength. Glue D̄₁ and D̄₂ along their boundaries via φ to form a closed topological surface Σ equipped with the natural length metric inherited from the planar metrics on D̄₁ and D̄₂. Let C ⊂ Σ be the image of C₁ (equivalently C₂) under the gluing.

It is known (via results of A. D. Aleksandrov and Yu. G. Reshetnyak in the theory of two-dimensional manifolds of bounded curvature) that every such isometric sewing is conformally admissible — i.e. Σ carries a natural conformal structure making it conformally equivalent to the Riemann sphere S² — and moreover the curve C, viewed on Σ ≅ S², is again a curve of bounded boundary rotation.

Problem. Give a purely function-theoretic (i.e. complex-analytic) proof of the following statement: under the above hypotheses, the curve C on the resulting Riemann sphere has bounded boundary rotation.

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published function-theoretic proof of the bounded-boundary-rotation property for the curve produced by isometric sewing of two Jordan domains with Paatero-bounded boundary rotation. The known proofs proceed via Aleksandrov–Reshetnyak's theory of two-dimensional manifolds of bounded curvature; no purely complex-analytic alternative was located in the available sources, so the status of Huber's request is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Functions of bounded boundary rotation
status_evidence.snippet: Classical reference on Paatero's class of functions of bounded boundary rotation; does not address Huber's sewing problem.
status_evidence.claim: Standard literature on bounded boundary rotation in function theory does not appear to give a function-theoretic proof of the sewing statement.

status_evidence.title: On functions of bounded boundary rotation I
status_evidence.snippet: Develops analytic properties of functions whose images have bounded boundary rotation, without treating isometric sewing.
status_evidence.claim: No function-theoretic resolution of Huber's question was identified in the located references.
